question: In which of the following places in India, the day temperature rises to 50° Celsius and drops down to near 15° Celsius the same night?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Thar Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, experiences extreme temperature variations due to its arid climate.
 
• Day temperatures in the Thar Desert can rise to as high as 50°C during summer, while nighttime temperatures can drop to near 15°C due to rapid heat loss.
 
• The desert’s sandy terrain has low heat retention capacity, causing significant temperature fluctuations between day and night.
 
• This extreme temperature variation is a characteristic feature of arid and semi-arid regions like the Thar Desert.
 
• The Thar Desert spans Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana in India, and also extends into Pakistan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Arid Climate:**

 
 
• Characterized by low annual rainfall, high evaporation rates, and extreme temperature fluctuations.
 
• Arid regions often experience very hot days and cool nights due to limited vegetation and moisture.
 
 
 
• **Heat Retention in Sand:**
 
 
• Sand has low heat retention capacity, meaning it heats up quickly during the day and cools rapidly at night.
 
• This property contributes to drastic temperature changes in desert areas.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Life in the Thar Desert:**
 
 
• Extreme temperatures make survival challenging for humans, animals, and plants.
 
• Flora and fauna in the region have adapted to these conditions, such as camels and drought-resistant plants.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Importance:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is the most densely populated desert in the world, with settlements relying on groundwater and scarce rainfall.
 
• It plays a significant role in India's cultural and economic activities, including tourism and mineral extraction.
